pathway.title: Penske Automotive Group, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Scale and mix put a floor under earnings. Dealerships and trucks produced 97.1% of revenue, service and parts earned 37.8% of 2025 gross profit on 10.6% of revenue, the U.S. supplied 62% of revenue and the U.K. 26%, and premium brands were 71% of automotive revenue; and EBITDA has stayed within USD 1,527.6 million to USD 1,539.0 million across 2024, 2025 and the last twelve months to September 2026, USD 1,533.6 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 60–61; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Margins, not volumes, show the pressure. EBITDA margin fell from 5.54% in 2023 to 4.71% over the last twelve months, a loss of 83 bp; gross profit per new vehicle fell 6.0% to USD 4,695, which the issuer attributes to a tariff-related pull-forward in the prior period, vehicle mix and affordability, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to 73.2% of gross profit from 71.5% while gross profit grew 0.2%. Revenue grew 3.1% in nine months, 2.00% excluding currency, but operating income fell 7.6%, so each point of lost gross profit costs about 3.4% of EBITDA before any cost response. Basis: calculation H3; calculation H4; calculation H6; calculation H10; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57, 64

- Cash generation covers the dividend but is falling and is being outspent. Free cash flow has fallen from USD 852.8 million in 2024 to USD 650.5 million in 2025 and USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months; in nine months it was USD 507.5 million, against USD 281.0 million of dividends, USD 26.3 million of repurchases and USD 518.0 million of net acquisitions, a shortfall of USD 317.8 million, and Total Debt rose USD 201.7 million from year end 2025. Operating cash flow fell USD 174.8 million, partly because an inventory build outran floor plan funding, so cash conversion depends on vehicle inventory and its financing staying in step. Basis: calculation H1; calculation H18; calculation G5; calculation G8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Leverage on the issuer's own measure is low, but vehicle claims sit outside it. Total Debt is 1.54x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest 5.49x, 6.05x on a like-for-like basis; adding floor plan notes payable lifts leverage to 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest, and operating lease liabilities of USD 2,509.8 million are on top. A 100 bp rate move would change annual interest expense by about USD 55.9 million, 3.6% of EBITDA. Basis: calculation G1; calculation G3; calculation G4; calculation H9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity covers the current structure but rests on few lenders and one nearly full line. Liquidity, measured as cash plus issuer-stated availability, is about USD 1,568.3 million; the three lenders to the U.S. credit agreement are manufacturer finance arms, the revolving mortgage facility is 99.9% drawn, and U.S. revolver borrowings rose USD 108.0 million between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-12. The largest printed maturity, USD 939.3 million in 2028, is 43.4% of debt at year end 2025 and is probably smaller now that the U.S. credit agreement expiry moved to 2029; the only bond is USD 500 million of 2029 notes. Basis: calculation G6; calculation H12; calculation H13; calculation G9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Earnings quality is the second risk: reported results lean on the equity investee and disposal gains. Penske Transportation Solutions supplied 17.0% of nine-month pre-tax earnings but paid 43.7% of its equity earnings in cash, its fleet is 14.1% smaller than the 2024 annual report stated, and retail automotive segment income excluding disposal gains fell 17.5%, while issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,458.8 million is level with USD 1,459.2 million at year end 2025. Basis: calculation G10; calculation G11; calculation G12; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

- The take-private is the primary credit risk. Penske Corporation and Mitsui, holders of 72.6%, propose to buy the rest at USD 212.00 per share with up to USD 2.2 billion of equity and up to USD 1.8 billion of debt; at the ceiling debt would be USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x EBITDA, and the equity may pay selling holders rather than add cash to the business. The controlling holders also sit on both sides of a USD 519.4 million related-party purchase in 2025, the manufacturers whose consent is not stated hold rights on a merger, and no covenant level is printed. Basis: calculation G2; calculation G7; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25, 90–91

runs.text: Strength one. Service and parts give the credit its steadiest earnings base. Retail automotive service and parts earned 37.8% of 2025 gross profit on 10.6% of revenue and retail truck service and parts a further 7.1%, so 44.9% of gross profit comes from work that follows vehicles already on the road rather than from new sales. That keeps gross profit and interest cover steadier when new vehicle margins fall, which supports debt service through a vehicle downturn. Basis: calculation H8; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9

Strength two. Debt is low against earnings on the issuer's own measure. Total Debt is 1.54x last-twelve-month EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest 5.49x, or 6.05x like-for-like, so earnings can fall a good way before leverage becomes a constraint, although covenant levels are not printed. Basis: calculation G1; calculation G3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength three. Free cash flow still funds the dividend, and spending is flexible. Free cash flow of USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months, down from USD 852.8 million in 2024, covered dividends of USD 372.1 million 1.34 times, and capital expenditure, about 1.02% of revenue, was cut from USD 386.0 million in 2023 to USD 324.6 million in 2025, a lever that can be pulled in stress. Basis: calculation H2; calculation H7; calculation H18; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength four. Earnings are spread across brands, countries and businesses, so a single market shock reaches only part of EBITDA. Premium brands were 71% of automotive revenue, the U.S. 62% of revenue and the U.K. 26%, truck retail 10.7% and Penske Australia 2.9%; in 2025 U.K. premium sales fell 6.8% and North American heavy truck sales fell 18.2%, yet EBITDA moved only 0.74%. Basis: calculation H14; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Strength five. Reporting and lender support aid monitoring. The 2025 statements carry unqualified audit opinions with effective internal control, liquidity is about USD 1,568.3 million, and the lenders under the U.S. credit agreement consented to the take-private, so near-term bank funding looks available on the printed evidence. Basis: calculation G6; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness one. The take-private could roughly double debt. At the ceiling, new debt of up to USD 1.8 billion would lift Total Debt to USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x EBITDA against 1.54x, with the holders of 72.6% on both sides of the deal, equity that may pay selling holders rather than reach the company, and the rate, ranking and maturity of the debt not stated. That would remove most of the room that the low leverage gives and raise refinancing risk. Basis: calculation G2; calculation G7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weakness two. Retail automotive profit and free cash flow are eroding. Segment income excluding disposal gains fell 17.5% to USD 531.6 million over nine months, free cash flow is 41.6% below 2024, gross profit per new vehicle fell 6.0%, selling, general and administrative expense rose to 73.2% of gross profit, and EBITDA margin has lost 83 bp since 2023, so each point of lost gross profit costs about 3.4% of EBITDA before any cost response. Basis: calculation G10; calculation H3; calculation H6; calculation H10; calculation H18; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12

Weakness three. Acquisitions and related-party spending outran cash generation, and book equity is soft. Nine-month free cash flow fell USD 317.8 million short of dividends, repurchases and net acquisitions, Total Debt rose USD 201.7 million, goodwill and franchise rights are 68.9% of book equity, and the two dealerships bought in 2026 earn a pre-tax return that implies a price of 21.7x, on top of a USD 519.4 million related-party purchase in 2025. Basis: calculation H1; calculation G13; calculation G14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness four. Claims outside the debt measure and one full facility narrow the margin. Including floor plan notes payable, debt is 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest, operating lease liabilities are USD 2,509.8 million, the revolving mortgage facility is 99.9% drawn, and the U.S. revolver rose USD 108.0 million after the quarter end, so the headline leverage understates the claims on cash flow. Basis: calculation G4; calculation H13; calculation G9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Weakness five. Manufacturers hold leverage over the structure and earnings lean on one investee. Franchise and framework agreements give manufacturers rights on a merger or change of control and the filings do not say whether consent is needed, while Penske Transportation Solutions supplied 17.0% of nine-month pre-tax earnings, paid 43.7% of its equity earnings in cash and runs a fleet 14.1% smaller than the 2024 annual report stated. Basis: calculation G10; calculation G11; calculation G12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 33–35

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: On 2026-10-15 the issuer agreed to be acquired by Motown Acquisition Corp., a vehicle owned by Penske Corporation and Mitsui, for USD 212.00 in cash per share, with the buyer merging into the issuer so that it survives as a private company owned about 64% by Penske Corporation and 36% by Mitsui. The issuer states an enterprise value of about USD 16.3 billion and expects to close in the first quarter of 2027, and either side may terminate if closing has not occurred by 2027-10-15. The issuer would owe the buyer USD 383.0 million in specified cases, including a superior proposal, and the buyer would owe the issuer USD 488.0 million in other specified cases; approval needs a majority of all shares and a majority of the votes cast by disinterested holders, and the holders of 72.6% have agreed to vote in favour. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10, 89; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

The buyer expects to fund the price and costs with up to USD 2.2 billion of equity from the two investors and up to USD 1.8 billion of debt committed by three banks, reduced by up to USD 1.8 billion of senior subordinated notes and by up to USD 1.1 billion of added borrowing under the U.S. credit agreement. The Thirteenth Amendment to that agreement, signed on 2026-10-15, lets the issuer raise its revolving commitment from USD 1.5 billion to as much as USD 2.4 billion, including up to USD 400.0 million that may be borrowed above the borrowing base, and permits up to USD 1.8 billion of new senior unsecured bridge borrowing of 364 days or senior subordinated notes. The increase takes effect only if the merger closes and at least USD 2.2 billion of equity is funded. At the ceiling the issuer's debt would be USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x last-twelve-month EBITDA, and the rate, ranking and maturity of the new debt are not stated. Basis: calculation A5; calculation A6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 90–91

The filings show no new notes issue in 2025 or 2026. The USD 550 million 3.50% notes were repaid at maturity on 2025-09-01, and the only note issue left is USD 500 million of 3.75% senior subordinated notes due 2029, guaranteed by the issuer's 100% owned U.S. subsidiaries. Debt added in 2026 sits in revolving and mortgage facilities: the U.S. revolver stood at USD 498.0 million on 2026-09-30 and USD 606.0 million on 2026-10-12, and the revolving mortgage facility was drawn to USD 598.0 million against a capacity of USD 598.4 million, after its maximum was raised to USD 750.0 million in July 2026. Basis: calculation A10; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed credit agreement or indenture is in the set, and the run settings declare no legal documents. The filings name the covenant tests of the U.S., U.K. and property lease agreements and state compliance at September 30, 2026, but none prints a threshold, a step-down or a reported covenant ratio, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated. Searches of all eight documents for covenant ratio levels found none for the issuer's own agreements; the only covenant-style level printed is the 3.0 to 1.0 debt-to-equity test in the Penske Transportation Solutions distribution terms. Remediation: add the credit agreements and the indenture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The set contains no credit rating, rating-agency report or rating trigger; the run settings list none, and the filings mention credit ratings only as a risk of the merger announcement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No market prices for the senior subordinated notes, the bank debt or the common stock were supplied, and the run settings list no quotes. The values printed are the USD 212.00 per share offer and the issuer's own fair value of its notes, which it labels as based on quoted prices for the identical liability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer financial data are supplied and the run settings name no peers; the 2025 annual report names five peer companies only for its stock performance graph.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquisition of Penske Motor Group on November 19, 2025 was accounted for as a common-control transaction and all comparative periods from the 2025 annual report onward were recast, so the 2024 annual report is not on the same basis: the calculations size the difference for 2024 revenue, net income, total assets and debt. Fiscal 2022 exists only on the original basis. The 2025 quarterly reports themselves are not supplied, so 2025 quarters appear only as recast comparatives.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The U.S. credit agreement's expiry is printed as September 30, 2027 in the 2024 annual report, September 30, 2028 in the 2025 annual report and the first two 2026 quarterly reports, and September 30, 2029 in the third quarter report, which does not say which amendment moved it. The latest printed term is used and the unexplained step is kept as a conflict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The third quarter report prints no maturity schedule; the last schedule is at December 31, 2025. A schedule at the latest balance sheet date is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Directors, executive officers, compensation and security ownership are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement, and no proxy statement is in the set. The 2025 annual report states approximate ownership of 52% by Penske Corporation affiliates and 20% by Mitsui.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No stand-alone financial statements of Penske Transportation Solutions, the 28.9% equity-method investment that makes up almost all of the equity-method balance, are in the set. The 2025 and 2024 annual reports print combined condensed income statement and balance sheet information for all equity-method investees, and the quarterly reports print none, so interim earnings, assets and debt of the partnership are not established; only the issuer's share of earnings, distributions received and carrying value are printed for the quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The releases and reports give qualitative outlook text but no quantified management guidance for 2026 or 2027, apart from the estimated annualized revenue of recently acquired dealerships stated in the first and second quarter releases, and those releases mention investor presentations that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is in the set, so events between that date and the as-of date are not covered; the revolver balance at October 12, 2026 is a post-quarter figure kept apart from September 30 figures.

fields.value: Financial foundation for Penske Automotive Group, Inc. (issuer pag-1019849), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage from fiscal 2023 to the quarter ended 2026-09-30, in USD millions on the recast basis that includes Penske Motor Group. The perimeter is the issuer's consolidated group; floor plan notes payable and operating lease liabilities are shown but sit outside Total Debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Penske Automotive Group's non-vehicle debt is modest, at 1.50x reported EBITDA after cash and with 5.49x interest cover at September 30, 2026, but the pending take-private could add debt that none of these figures include.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R1; calculation R2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11, 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Floor plan notes payable of USD 4,262.0 million and operating lease liabilities of USD 2,509.8 million sit outside that debt, and counting floor plan lifts leverage to 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest. Net debt was USD 2,298.9 million, or USD 2,394.8 million pro forma for the dividend payable on December 1, 2026, and liquidity was about USD 1,568.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R6; calculation N5; calculation X2; calculation LQ5; calculation Z4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Net leverage rose from 1.15x at year end 2024 to 1.38x at year end 2025 and peaked at 1.69x on March 31, 2026, after USD 669.7 million of acquisitions paid in cash, then fell to 1.50x by September 30, 2026 as total debt fell by USD 269.7 million and last-twelve-month EBITDA edged up to USD 1,533.6 million. The improvement comes from repaying debt, not from earnings growth: issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,458.8 million is level with USD 1,459.2 million at year end 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R1; calculation R4; calculation R5; calculation Z1; calculation L6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover has held between 5.43x and 5.63x across the five balance-sheet dates, but the measure mixes perimeters: cash interest paid of USD 279.2 million over the last twelve months is close to floor plan plus other interest expense of USD 274.4 million, so it evidently includes floor plan interest that EBITDA is already struck after. On a like-for-like basis, EBITDA before floor plan interest covered cash interest 6.05x over the last twelve months. The pressure point is other interest expense, USD 117.9 million over the last twelve months against USD 91.6 million in 2025, because revolver borrowing paid for dealership acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R2; calculation R8; calculation L16; calculation K3; calculation Z2; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow was USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months and USD 507.5 million in the first nine months of 2026, which covered dividends of USD 281.0 million with USD 226.5 million to spare. Operating cash flow fell USD 174.8 million to USD 724.6 million: a USD 244.2 million inventory build was only partly funded by a USD 110.8 million rise in floor plan payable, and lower net income and a larger non-cash disposal gain made up most of the rest, so the cash conversion of EBITDA depends on inventory and floor plan funding staying in step. Net borrowing under revolver and mortgage facilities of USD 347.4 million helped fund the acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation Z2; calculation Z3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported EBITDA of USD 1,207.6 million for the first nine months of 2026 includes USD 166.4 million of equity earnings from affiliates, led by Penske Transportation Solutions, which paid USD 73.0 million in cash distributions, and a USD 90.9 million gain on dealership sales. Issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,129.7 million was flat on USD 1,130.1 million a year earlier, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to 73.2% of gross profit from 71.5%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was cash of USD 68.3 million plus about USD 1,500 million of issuer-stated borrowing availability, USD 1,568.3 million in all. The last printed maturity schedule, at December 31, 2025, put USD 939.3 million of debt in 2028, the largest year, but the printed expiry of the U.S. credit agreement has since moved from 2028 to 2029, so the 2028 wall is probably smaller today; no current schedule is printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation LQ5; calculation M1; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 143–144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 67

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the benign leverage reading is that vehicle floor plan and leases are real claims that the issuer's non-vehicle measure leaves out. Counting floor plan notes payable lifts leverage to 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest, against 3.69x at year end 2025, and operating lease liabilities of USD 2,509.8 million are on top. The second case is the transaction: committed debt financing of up to USD 1.8 billion, of which up to USD 1.1 billion could be added to the U.S. credit agreement, comes with a termination fee of USD 383.0 million that the issuer would owe in specified circumstances, and the financing that becomes the issuer's own debt at closing is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation R6; calculation R7; calculation Z4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 25, 90–91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The benign reading would be overturned by a printed covenant threshold with thin headroom, a fall in adjusted EBITDA while debt stays at today's level, or a financing structure at closing that adds most of the committed debt to the issuer's balance sheet. It would be confirmed by a maturity schedule at the latest balance sheet date that shows the extended revolver and no new near-term wall.

Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the split of cash paid for interest.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The relative ranking of the secured facilities and the subordination terms of the senior subordinated notes and the related-party note are not in the sources, so ranks 1 and 2 follow the stated security and the issuer's description only. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The take-private financing is stated as maximums (equity up to USD 2.2 billion, debt up to USD 1.8 billion, up to USD 1.1 billion through the U.S. credit agreement), and no source states the debt that becomes the issuer's own at closing, so no pro forma net debt or leverage for the transaction is established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the merger agreement, commitment letters and the amendment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The U.S. credit agreement revolver balance of USD 606.0 million at 2026-10-12 is stated but cash at that date is not, so its effect on net debt is not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain cash at that date or the next quarter's balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No covenant threshold or reported covenant ratio for the U.S. credit agreement, the U.K. credit agreement or the property leases is printed, so covenant headroom cannot be calculated from these tables. Severity: Medium, because it restricts covenant analysis rather than these tables. Action: obtain the credit agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue and capital expenditure for the Non-Automotive Investments segment are printed as dashes and no corporate or elimination line is printed; the three revenue-bearing segments add to consolidated revenue in every period, so no segment sum is stated for the investments segment. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The balance sheet at 2023-12-31 recast for Penske Motor Group, the recast operating lease liabilities at year end 2024 and the current operating lease liabilities at year end 2024 are not printed, so lease liabilities are shown for year end 2025 and 2026-09-30 only. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Penske Automotive Group, Inc. (issuer pag-1019849), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway: what the company does, who controls it, the pending take-private, related-party dealings, capital allocation and the sponsor and governance risk level. It draws on the annual reports for 2024 and 2025, the three 2026 quarterly reports and three 2026 earnings releases, in USD millions unless stated, on the recast basis that includes Penske Motor Group from 2025-11-19.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and sponsor risk is Medium: Penske Corporation and Mitsui, holders of 72.6% of the shares, propose a take-private that could add up to USD 1.8 billion of company debt to USD 2,367.2 million today. At that ceiling, debt would be 2.72x last-twelve-month EBITDA, against 1.54x now.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The dealership and truck businesses are diversified, the filings show no priming, exchange or other creditor-adverse step, and the U.S. credit agreement lenders consented to the deal. The risk is that the controlling holders sit on both sides of the buyout, paid USD 519.4 million to related parties for Penske Motor Group in 2025, and that the debt left at the company is not yet established; the level moves to High if most of the committed debt lands there.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control rests with Penske Corporation and Mitsui and is fixed by contract to March 2030, so the board's makeup is set by the same two groups that are now the buyer. The two hold 52.3% and 20.3% of the shares; under the stockholders agreement Mitsui votes for up to fourteen directors that Penske Corporation votes for, and the Chair and Chief Executive Officer holds the same posts at Penske Corporation. A voting agreement caps the discretionary votes of Penske Corporation and the Chair at 43.57% of the shares, and a special committee of independent directors negotiated the deal, with a majority of disinterested holders also required to approve it; those steps protect minority shareholders but give creditors no vote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The take-private is a debt-assisted buyout with the controlling holders on the buy side, and existing creditors gain no exit right. The price is USD 212.00 per share, USD 2.00 or 0.95% above the proposal made 85 days earlier, and about USD 3.8 billion is payable to the 27.4% of shares the investors do not hold; the buyer plans up to USD 2.2 billion of equity and up to USD 1.8 billion of debt. The issuer states the deal is not a change of control under the mortgage facilities, or under the 3.75% notes if technical requirements are met, so no 101% repurchase right arises, and the lenders under the U.S. credit agreement gave a limited consent and a waiver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A1; calculation A2; calculation A4; calculation A6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25–26, 28, 90–91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - One related-party transaction is large, and the filings do not show how it was priced or approved. In 2025 the issuer bought Penske Motor Group for USD 519.4 million from affiliates of Penske Corporation and from an entity controlled by an affiliate of the Vice Chair, paying USD 363.6 million in cash and USD 155.8 million in a 4.50% subordinated note that the issuer guarantees, and USD 401.7 million was charged to retained earnings; the price was 10.75x the business's USD 48.3 million of 2025 net income, which carried no income tax because it was a pass-through partnership. Routine fees, rent and asset sales with Penske Corporation and its affiliates were small, about USD 14.7 million in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B4; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 119, 148–150

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Dividends are rising while repurchases have fallen away, and no dividend is described as funded by borrowing, which is neutral for creditors but fixes a growing claim. Dividends were USD 281.0 million in the first nine months of 2026, up from USD 252.7 million a year earlier; the quarterly rate rose every quarter from USD 1.22 in early 2025 to an announced USD 1.46, and the merger agreement lets it keep rising by at most USD 0.02 a quarter. Repurchases were USD 26.3 million against USD 119.0 million a year earlier and stopped in the third quarter, and the merger agreement restricts further repurchases. Penske Corporation and Mitsui receive about 72.6% of each dividend, USD 69.6 million of the December payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A8; calculation C1; calculation C2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 68, 75, 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition spending in 2026 was large and mostly paid for franchise rights, so book equity is a softer cushion than it looks. Two U.S. dealerships bought in the first quarter cost USD 669.7 million, of which USD 537.6 million (80.3%) was booked as indefinite-lived intangibles; their third-quarter pre-tax income of USD 7.7 million annualises to USD 30.8 million, a price of 21.7x. Goodwill and franchise rights are now 68.9% of book equity against 64.5% at year end 2025, and other interest expense rose 39.8% to USD 92.4 million over nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating risk is moderated by mix, but in 2026 the equity investee and disposal gains are holding up profit that the dealerships alone are not. Service and parts earn 45.5% of retail automotive gross profit at a 59.3% margin, yet retail automotive segment income excluding disposal gains fell 17.5% to USD 531.6 million over nine months and the new vehicle gross margin slipped to 8.6% from 9.2%. Penske Transportation Solutions supplied 15.3% of 2025 pre-tax earnings, and the non-automotive segment it dominates earned USD 166.4 million in nine months, but it paid 43.7% of its nine-month equity earnings in cash before its November distribution, and its managed fleet is 14.1% smaller than the 2024 annual report stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 70

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Manufacturers hold as much practical control as the shareholders, and the filings do not say whether the take-private needs their consent. Franchise agreements can be terminated or not renewed, framework agreements give manufacturers rights on a merger, a change of control, an acquisition of 20% of the voting stock or a material change in capital structure, and the agreements with BMW, the largest U.K. brand, expire in December 2026. The three lenders under the U.S. credit agreement are the finance arms of Mercedes-Benz, Toyota and Daimler Truck, so the same manufacturers sit on both sides of the relationship.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reporting and audit are a strength, with gaps around the deal. The statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control, no material legal proceedings are reported, and related-party fees are reviewed by the Audit Committee; against that, the internal control audit excluded the related-party acquisition, the issuer will hold no earnings call during the deal, and no covenant level is printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower risk level is that nothing in the record shows the controlling holders taking value from creditors: no exchange, drop-down or non-pro-rata step appears, the lenders consented, the investors plan up to USD 2.2 billion of new equity beside up to USD 1.8 billion of debt, and at the ceiling the debt would equal about 25.6% of the USD 16.3 billion enterprise value the issuer states at the offer price. The strongest case for a higher risk level is that the equity money pays selling holders and not the company, so the extra debt would add leverage without adding cash to the business, and the rate, ranking and maturity of that debt are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A5; calculation A6; calculation A7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 90–91; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to Low if executed documents place most of the new debt outside the company's guarantor group or cut the committed amount. It would move to High if the full USD 1.8 billion lands on the company under a bridge of 364 days, if a manufacturer withholds consent, or if the arrangement under which Penske Corporation has agreed to pledge shares for a loan facility is triggered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The merger agreement, the debt commitment letters and the credit agreement amendment are described by the issuer but not supplied, so the debt that becomes the company's, its ranking, rate and maturity cannot be fixed and the 2.72x figure is a ceiling, not a forecast, and the Medium level could move either way once they are seen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not in the set, so board independence, committee membership, pay and the related-party approval policy are not established; if they show independent oversight of insider dealings, the Medium level could be Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - How the price of Penske Motor Group was set and who approved it are not described, so whether USD 519.4 million was a fair price is not established and the related-party conclusion rests on the amount and the parties alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No restricted payment, investment or related-party covenant level is printed, so what the controlling holders may take out of the company cannot be separated from what they have done, and no conclusion on legal capacity is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The record covers filings from the 2024 annual report onward, so any creditor-adverse or related-party episode before 2022 is outside this assessment, and the finances and intentions of Penske Corporation and Mitsui are not in the sources, so their willingness to support or extract is not inferred from who they are.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-10-15 the issuer agreed to be acquired by Motown Acquisition Corp., a vehicle owned by Penske Corporation and Mitsui, for USD 212.00 in cash per share, with the buyer merging into the issuer so that it survives as a private company owned about 64% by Penske Corporation and 36% by Mitsui. The issuer states an enterprise value of about USD 16.3 billion and expects to close in the first quarter of 2027, and either side may terminate if closing has not occurred by 2027-10-15. The issuer would owe the buyer USD 383.0 million in specified cases, including a superior proposal, and the buyer would owe the issuer USD 488.0 million in other specified cases; approval needs a majority of all shares and a majority of the votes cast by disinterested holders, and the holders of 72.6% have agreed to vote in favour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The buyer expects to fund the price and costs with up to USD 2.2 billion of equity from the two investors and up to USD 1.8 billion of debt committed by three banks, reduced by up to USD 1.8 billion of senior subordinated notes and by up to USD 1.1 billion of added borrowing under the U.S. credit agreement. The Thirteenth Amendment to that agreement, signed on 2026-10-15, lets the issuer raise its revolving commitment from USD 1.5 billion to as much as USD 2.4 billion, including up to USD 400.0 million that may be borrowed above the borrowing base, and permits up to USD 1.8 billion of new senior unsecured bridge borrowing of 364 days or senior subordinated notes. The increase takes effect only if the merger closes and at least USD 2.2 billion of equity is funded. At the ceiling the issuer's debt would be USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x last-twelve-month EBITDA, and the rate, ranking and maturity of the new debt are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A5; calculation A6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 90–91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings show no new notes issue in 2025 or 2026. The USD 550 million 3.50% notes were repaid at maturity on 2025-09-01, and the only note issue left is USD 500 million of 3.75% senior subordinated notes due 2029, guaranteed by the issuer's 100% owned U.S. subsidiaries. Debt added in 2026 sits in revolving and mortgage facilities: the U.S. revolver stood at USD 498.0 million on 2026-09-30 and USD 606.0 million on 2026-10-12, and the revolving mortgage facility was drawn to USD 598.0 million against a capacity of USD 598.4 million, after its maximum was raised to USD 750.0 million in July 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. It is driven by concentrated control, a pending buyout by those holders and a large related-party purchase, because they place the setting of leverage and distributions with holders who are also the buyers, which implies higher refinancing and monitoring risk; countervailing evidence is the absence of any priming, exchange or non-pro-rata step and the lenders' consent. Further analysis requires the financing documents and covenant text.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Penske Automotive Group, Inc. (issuer pag-1019849), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway: business quality, cash conversion, leverage, liquidity, refinancing, governance and the primary downside path. It combines the filings and releases with the supplied analyses of sources, financials and business, in USD millions unless stated, on the recast basis that includes Penske Motor Group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is adequate: service and parts, earning 37.8% of 2025 gross profit, support EBITDA near USD 1,533.6 million against debt of 1.54x, but the controlling holders' take-private could lift debt to 2.72x, so its financing is the main credit risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G1; calculation G2; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow of USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months, down 41.6% from USD 852.8 million in 2024, still covered dividends of USD 372.1 million 1.34 times, but nine-month net acquisitions of USD 518.0 million exceeded the free cash flow left after dividends and repurchases, and retail automotive profit excluding disposal gains is falling. Liquidity of about USD 1,568.3 million fits the current structure; the downside is the deal debt arriving while earnings soften.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G5; calculation H1; calculation H2; calculation H18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Scale and mix put a floor under earnings. Dealerships and trucks produced 97.1% of revenue, service and parts earned 37.8% of 2025 gross profit on 10.6% of revenue, the U.S. supplied 62% of revenue and the U.K. 26%, and premium brands were 71% of automotive revenue; and EBITDA has stayed within USD 1,527.6 million to USD 1,539.0 million across 2024, 2025 and the last twelve months to September 2026, USD 1,533.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins, not volumes, show the pressure. EBITDA margin fell from 5.54% in 2023 to 4.71% over the last twelve months, a loss of 83 bp; gross profit per new vehicle fell 6.0% to USD 4,695, which the issuer attributes to a tariff-related pull-forward in the prior period, vehicle mix and affordability, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to 73.2% of gross profit from 71.5% while gross profit grew 0.2%. Revenue grew 3.1% in nine months, 2.00% excluding currency, but operating income fell 7.6%, so each point of lost gross profit costs about 3.4% of EBITDA before any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H3; calculation H4; calculation H6; calculation H10; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56–57, 64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation covers the dividend but is falling and is being outspent. Free cash flow has fallen from USD 852.8 million in 2024 to USD 650.5 million in 2025 and USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months; in nine months it was USD 507.5 million, against USD 281.0 million of dividends, USD 26.3 million of repurchases and USD 518.0 million of net acquisitions, a shortfall of USD 317.8 million, and Total Debt rose USD 201.7 million from year end 2025. Operating cash flow fell USD 174.8 million, partly because an inventory build outran floor plan funding, so cash conversion depends on vehicle inventory and its financing staying in step.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H1; calculation H18; calculation G5; calculation G8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage on the issuer's own measure is low, but vehicle claims sit outside it. Total Debt is 1.54x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest 5.49x, 6.05x on a like-for-like basis; adding floor plan notes payable lifts leverage to 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest, and operating lease liabilities of USD 2,509.8 million are on top. A 100 bp rate move would change annual interest expense by about USD 55.9 million, 3.6% of EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G1; calculation G3; calculation G4; calculation H9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity covers the current structure but rests on few lenders and one nearly full line. Liquidity, measured as cash plus issuer-stated availability, is about USD 1,568.3 million; the three lenders to the U.S. credit agreement are manufacturer finance arms, the revolving mortgage facility is 99.9% drawn, and U.S. revolver borrowings rose USD 108.0 million between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-12. The largest printed maturity, USD 939.3 million in 2028, is 43.4% of debt at year end 2025 and is probably smaller now that the U.S. credit agreement expiry moved to 2029; the only bond is USD 500 million of 2029 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G6; calculation H12; calculation H13; calculation G9; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings quality is the second risk: reported results lean on the equity investee and disposal gains. Penske Transportation Solutions supplied 17.0% of nine-month pre-tax earnings but paid 43.7% of its equity earnings in cash, its fleet is 14.1% smaller than the 2024 annual report stated, and retail automotive segment income excluding disposal gains fell 17.5%, while issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,458.8 million is level with USD 1,459.2 million at year end 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G10; calculation G11; calculation G12; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The take-private is the primary credit risk. Penske Corporation and Mitsui, holders of 72.6%, propose to buy the rest at USD 212.00 per share with up to USD 2.2 billion of equity and up to USD 1.8 billion of debt; at the ceiling debt would be USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x EBITDA, and the equity may pay selling holders rather than add cash to the business. The controlling holders also sit on both sides of a USD 519.4 million related-party purchase in 2025, the manufacturers whose consent is not stated hold rights on a merger, and no covenant level is printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G2; calculation G7; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 25, 90–91

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that even the ceiling case leaves debt at 2.72x EBITDA and about 25.6% of the USD 16.3 billion enterprise value the issuer states, the investors are committing new equity, lenders have consented, and EBITDA moved only 0.74% between 2024 and 2025 through a weak truck cycle and a falling U.K. premium market. The strongest case for a worse view is that a repeat of the 2023 to 2025 EBITDA decline of 10.74% would take current debt to 1.73x but ceiling debt to 3.04x, with interest cost, ranking and maturity of the new debt not stated and the three lenders to the main facility also the manufacturers whose consent is open.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G2; calculation G7; calculation H11; calculation H14; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if executed documents put most of the new debt outside the company or cut the committed amount, and would weaken if the full USD 1.8 billion is drawn under a short bridge, if gross profit per new vehicle keeps falling while selling, general and administrative expense stays near 73.2% of gross profit, or if the mortgage line stays fully drawn while acquisitions continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer, rating or market pricing is supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged issuers in the sector and the word adequate rests on the issuer's own record; a weaker peer set would make it better, a stronger one worse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside is an analyst illustration that repeats the observed 2023 to 2025 EBITDA decline, using 2023 EBITDA calculated on the issuer's definition, and no forecast or management guidance is supplied, so it shows size and direction but not likelihood.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity availability is the issuer's rounded statement and the maturity schedule is printed only for year end 2025, so the refinancing view assumes the extended U.S. credit agreement has removed most of the 2028 maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels are not printed, so the liquidity and refinancing views assume compliance, as the issuer states, and cannot show headroom if earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Floor plan interest is partly offset by manufacturer credits and the split of cash interest paid is not printed, so interest cover is shown on two bases and the lower one is a conservative bound.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength one. Service and parts give the credit its steadiest earnings base. Retail automotive service and parts earned 37.8% of 2025 gross profit on 10.6% of revenue and retail truck service and parts a further 7.1%, so 44.9% of gross profit comes from work that follows vehicles already on the road rather than from new sales. That keeps gross profit and interest cover steadier when new vehicle margins fall, which supports debt service through a vehicle downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength two. Debt is low against earnings on the issuer's own measure. Total Debt is 1.54x last-twelve-month EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest 5.49x, or 6.05x like-for-like, so earnings can fall a good way before leverage becomes a constraint, although covenant levels are not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G1; calculation G3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength three. Free cash flow still funds the dividend, and spending is flexible. Free cash flow of USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months, down from USD 852.8 million in 2024, covered dividends of USD 372.1 million 1.34 times, and capital expenditure, about 1.02% of revenue, was cut from USD 386.0 million in 2023 to USD 324.6 million in 2025, a lever that can be pulled in stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H2; calculation H7; calculation H18; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength four. Earnings are spread across brands, countries and businesses, so a single market shock reaches only part of EBITDA. Premium brands were 71% of automotive revenue, the U.S. 62% of revenue and the U.K. 26%, truck retail 10.7% and Penske Australia 2.9%; in 2025 U.K. premium sales fell 6.8% and North American heavy truck sales fell 18.2%, yet EBITDA moved only 0.74%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H14; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength five. Reporting and lender support aid monitoring. The 2025 statements carry unqualified audit opinions with effective internal control, liquidity is about USD 1,568.3 million, and the lenders under the U.S. credit agreement consented to the take-private, so near-term bank funding looks available on the printed evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G6; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 110, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness one. The take-private could roughly double debt. At the ceiling, new debt of up to USD 1.8 billion would lift Total Debt to USD 4,167.2 million, 2.72x EBITDA against 1.54x, with the holders of 72.6% on both sides of the deal, equity that may pay selling holders rather than reach the company, and the rate, ranking and maturity of the debt not stated. That would remove most of the room that the low leverage gives and raise refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G2; calculation G7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness two. Retail automotive profit and free cash flow are eroding. Segment income excluding disposal gains fell 17.5% to USD 531.6 million over nine months, free cash flow is 41.6% below 2024, gross profit per new vehicle fell 6.0%, selling, general and administrative expense rose to 73.2% of gross profit, and EBITDA margin has lost 83 bp since 2023, so each point of lost gross profit costs about 3.4% of EBITDA before any cost response.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G10; calculation H3; calculation H6; calculation H10; calculation H18; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness three. Acquisitions and related-party spending outran cash generation, and book equity is soft. Nine-month free cash flow fell USD 317.8 million short of dividends, repurchases and net acquisitions, Total Debt rose USD 201.7 million, goodwill and franchise rights are 68.9% of book equity, and the two dealerships bought in 2026 earn a pre-tax return that implies a price of 21.7x, on top of a USD 519.4 million related-party purchase in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H1; calculation G13; calculation G14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness four. Claims outside the debt measure and one full facility narrow the margin. Including floor plan notes payable, debt is 3.92x EBITDA before floor plan interest, operating lease liabilities are USD 2,509.8 million, the revolving mortgage facility is 99.9% drawn, and the U.S. revolver rose USD 108.0 million after the quarter end, so the headline leverage understates the claims on cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G4; calculation H13; calculation G9; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness five. Manufacturers hold leverage over the structure and earnings lean on one investee. Franchise and framework agreements give manufacturers rights on a merger or change of control and the filings do not say whether consent is needed, while Penske Transportation Solutions supplied 17.0% of nine-month pre-tax earnings, paid 43.7% of its equity earnings in cash and runs a fleet 14.1% smaller than the 2024 annual report stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G10; calculation G11; calculation G12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 22, 33–35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a franchised dealer group that retails new and used vehicles, finance and insurance products, service and parts and commercial trucks, distributes trucks and power systems in Australia and New Zealand, and owns 28.9% of a truck leasing and logistics business. Retail automotive was 86.4% of 2025 revenue, retail trucks 10.7% and distribution 2.9%. Customers are mostly individual consumers and fleets with no stated concentration, but supply, floor plan assistance and warranty reimbursement all come from manufacturers, so cash generation is durable in service and parts and dependent on manufacturers for new vehicles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G15; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 35; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Penske Corporation and Mitsui hold 52.3% and 20.3% of the shares, contract to elect the board together until 2030, and are the proposed buyers; the notes are guaranteed only by the 100% owned U.S. subsidiaries, which produced 59.3% of 2025 revenue, so about 40.7% of revenue sits outside the guarantor group. Dividends are rising, repurchases have stopped, acquisitions are lumpy and large, and a related-party purchase in 2025 cost USD 519.4 million; the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G14; calculation G16; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, discretionary and priced by manufacturers rather than contracted. New vehicles were 45.4% of retail automotive revenue in nine months and used vehicles 34.2%; new retail units fell 2.4% while revenue per new retail unit rose 2.8%, yet gross profit per unit fell, so price increases flowed to manufacturers and not to the issuer. Service and parts, 12.2% of revenue, is recurring in nature and grew 2.7%, retail truck revenue grew 2.2%, and Penske Australia grew 21.4%, or 11.1% excluding currency, on standby power demand from data systems customers. Reported revenue grew 3.1%, or 2.00% excluding currency.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H4; calculation H6; calculation O1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against falling unit profit. The issuer states that most selling expenses are variable and a significant part of general and administrative expense is within its control, and floor plan interest fell 10.9% to USD 115.1 million on lower rates, while manufacturers' floor plan credits were USD 50.8 million. Against that, selling, general and administrative expense is 73.2% of gross profit, personnel expense alone 43.5%, and rent 8.7%, so operating margin slipped to 3.8% from 4.2% on gross margin of 16.1% against 16.5%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation O2; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low: capital expenditure was about 1.02% of 2025 revenue and 0.88% in nine months of 2026, and free cash flow was USD 497.9 million over the last twelve months, 32.5% of EBITDA. Conversion is exposed to vehicle inventory and its financing, because operating cash flow fell USD 174.8 million in nine months, and after dividends the USD 226.5 million of free cash flow that remained in nine months was smaller than the USD 518.0 million of net acquisitions. Cash conversion therefore supports debt service but not debt-funded growth at the 2026 pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H7; calculation H15; calculation G5; calculation G8; calculation G13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power is the strongest of the five competitive forces: manufacturers provide the vehicles exclusively, decide franchise renewal and hold rights on a change of control, which can remove revenue for a dealer with no alternative source. Rivalry among franchised dealers and manufacturers that sell directly, including agency models where units rose 9.2% in nine months, caps new vehicle margins; buyers are mostly price-aware individuals; online used sellers and private sales are partial substitutes; new entrants are electric vehicle makers selling directly. Together they help explain thin new vehicle margins of 8.6% and a gross profit that is not expanding.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Among external factors, tariffs, the U.K. zero emission mandate of 33% of new car sales in 2026, a U.K. vehicle finance redress scheme, currency and interest rates matter to credit: a 10% move in average exchange rates changes revenue by about USD 1.0 billion, the issuer's new U.S. electric vehicle sales fell 48.8%, and the issuer says the share of Chinese manufacturers in the U.K. grew from 8.7% to 17.5% in nine months. A credit-translated SWOT therefore reads: strengths in service and parts, low non-vehicle leverage and free cash flow; weaknesses in manufacturer dependence, thin new vehicle margins and soft book equity; opportunities in a truck replacement cycle with a backlog 21.1% above year end; threats in U.K. premium pressure and the take-private debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H16; calculation H17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39, 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 26–27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects lower U.S. electric vehicle sales, a challenging U.K. market, strong service and parts demand from an ageing vehicle base, an improving truck market with orders placed ahead of the 2027 emissions rules, firm energy systems orders in Australia and a smaller rental fleet at its equity investee. U.S. industry new light vehicle sales fell 2.0% in nine months, U.K. registrations rose 10.2%, and the truck backlog is 21.1% above year end, so near-term revenue is supported but unit profit is not. Over three to five years the electric vehicle transition in the U.K., agency selling and freight cycles at the equity investee are the factors that decide whether margins recover; the closing of the take-private, expected in the first quarter of 2027, decides leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H17; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_q326exhibit99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most credible downside is a repeat of the margin squeeze of 2023 to 2025 while the take-private debt arrives. Initiating condition: gross profit per new vehicle keeps falling, as it did 15.9% from 2023 to 2025, and U.K. premium and U.S. affordability weaken unit sales. First break: selling, general and administrative expense at 73.2% of gross profit, only partly variable, turns each 1% of lost gross profit into 3.4% of lost EBITDA before any cost response. Financial transmission: a decline matching the 10.74% seen from 2023 to 2025 would cut last-twelve-month EBITDA to USD 1,368.9 million, lifting debt to 1.73x today and 3.04x at the ceiling, while a 100 bp rate rise adds about USD 55.9 million of interest. Levers: capital expenditure, repurchases already stopped, disposals that raised USD 151.7 million, and dividend increases that insiders, who receive 72.6%, control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation H6; calculation H9; calculation H10; calculation H11; calculation G2; 10-K_2025-12-31_pag-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_pag-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 75, 85–86

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the current structure, since liquidity is about USD 1,568.3 million and debt would stay under 2x, but not clearly so at the ceiling, where leverage above 3x would depend on bridge refinancing terms that are not stated and on lenders that are also the manufacturers. Observable triggers are set out in the monitoring register.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G6; calculation H11; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Penske Automotive Group presents an adequate business profile supported by a service and parts earnings base, low non-vehicle leverage and free cash flow that still covers the dividend, but credit quality is constrained by eroding retail automotive profit, acquisitions that outran cash generation and controlling holders who are also the proposed buyers. Cash flow durability appears adequate but weakening, with USD 497.9 million of free cash flow over the last twelve months against USD 852.8 million in 2024. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the terms of the take-private debt, the extended U.S. credit agreement and the manufacturer finance arms that lend under it. The primary downside path is up to USD 1.8 billion of new debt arriving while unit profit falls. Further analysis would require the financing documents, covenant levels, peer data and the manufacturers' consent position. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: the financing of the take-private.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation G2; calculation G5; calculation H18; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
